issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify a constructor SealSaloon(String) (the constructor should take the saloon name), but the provided solution implements a no-argument constructor SealSaloon(). The template Main also instantiates SealSaloon with a no-arg constructor. This mismatch between the specification and the implemented/templated constructor signature can confuse students about which constructor to implement and may cause tests or example code to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor requirement consistent across artifacts. Either update the problem statement and UML to require a no-arg constructor (and document the saloon name is optional or stored elsewhere), or change the solution and template Main to use and demonstrate SealSaloon(String name). The preferred fix is to implement SealSaloon(String name) in the solution and update Main to call new SealSaloon("name"), so the implementation matches the UML and textual specification.

issues.description: The problem text instructs students to initialize default values (e.g., an empty orders array or a new Stock object) in the SealSaloon constructor, but later explicitly requires the stock attribute to be static (shared across instances). Initializing a static shared stock inside an instance constructor is contradictory guidance. The solution declares and initializes the static stock at field declaration. This inconsistency in where/how 'stock' should be initialized can confuse students about whether 'stock' is instance-level or static and where initialization should occur.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the specification: either (A) require stock to be a static attribute and state that it should be initialized at declaration (or in a static initializer) rather than the instance constructor, or (B) if initialization must occur in the constructor, change the requirement and UML so that stock is an instance (non-static) field. Update the problem statement to explicitly state how and where the shared stock should be initialized to avoid ambiguity.

issues.description: The problem statement specifies a constructor SealSaloon(String) (UML and textual description) but both the provided template usage (Main.java) and the reference solution implement and use a no-argument constructor SealSaloon(). This constructor-signature mismatch between the problem description and the code artifacts can confuse students about the required API and which constructor to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor requirement consistent across artifacts. Either (A) update the solution and template to provide and use a constructor matching the problem statement: public SealSaloon(String name) { this.orders = new Meal[]{}; /* optionally store name */ } and update Main to call new SealSaloon("SaloonName"); or (B) update the problem statement to require a no-argument constructor SealSaloon() (and remove the textual UML constructor signature) so it matches the provided template and solution.
